The graph above shows the curve $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ and the line $y=1.$ Find the $x$-coordinate of the point $B.$

$$

$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The $y$-values of both functions are the same at the intersection point. Equating the two equations gives: 

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=1
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arctan}⁡(1)=\frac{\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This value lies inside $0\le x\le 2\pi $ hence, our first solution is ${x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$ This is the $x$ coordinate of $A.$

To get another solution, we add $\pi $ to the principal value. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}=\pi +{x}_{1}=\pi +\frac{\pi }{4}=\frac{5\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the $x$-coordinate of $B$ is $\frac{5\pi }{4}.$
